First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x
$$

Also, recall the Pythagorean formula for sines and cosines:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1
$$

Using the above identities, we can simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)+{tan}^{2}⁡x & =1+{tan}^{2}⁡x \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$
